review_scope_note: Unlike prior API-based reviews that saw only the finding text, this audit had full repository access: experiment kernels, archived run logs/CSVs, prior reviews, remediations, and paper/CERTIFICATE.md where applicable. Quantitative claims were checked against primary artifacts; arithmetic and hashes were recomputed where feasible. No computational result was invented.
verification_methods: Checked data/class-numbers run logs for [1e9,1e10) and [1e10,1e11) histograms
Reviewed genus-theory correction of the 75.4% misreading

claim_reviews.evidence: run_1e9_1e10.log / _v2.log match the stated histogram bins.

claim_reviews.claim: Cohen–Lenstra: Pr(h=1)→0 for real quadratics; 75.4% is Pr(h_odd=1), not Pr(h=1).
claim_reviews.evidence: Genus theory forces 2-part structure; the corrected interpretation is the scientifically important part of this finding.

claim_reviews.claim: 27B range completed in ~4.5h on 8×B200 at ~1.7M disc/s.
claim_reviews.evidence: run_1e10_1e11_v2.log reports ~90666s (~25.2h) at ~301731 disc/sec on 5 GPU shards — not 4.5h/8-GPU/1.7M/s.

claim_reviews.claim: PARI subsample exact match / small-d historical rates.
claim_reviews.evidence: Stated but no validation artifact in the checkout.

claim_reviews.claim: HF README / older text implying upturn to 75.4% as Pr(h=1).
claim_reviews.evidence: Conflicts with the corrected finding; stale cards should be fixed.

missing_references: Runtime claim aligned to the actual completion log
overall_assessment: Billion-scale class-number histograms with a correct genus-theory interpretation of Cohen–Lenstra are a genuine contribution. The runtime claim does not match the completion log, and validation/HF-card hygiene remain weak. Silver is still earned by the histogram evidence and the conceptual correction.
recommendations: Replace 4.5h/1.7M/s with the log's 25.2h / 0.30M/s (or publish a different run that matches 4.5h)
certification_justification: Large-scale computation grounded in classical Cohen–Lenstra / genus theory, with log-backed histograms. Runtime and card nits do not destroy the core result.
